title: Lesson 64 - Can We Agree on This Much?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: We’ve compared the options, explored the two-stage idea and reviewed the small test. Can we agree on this much: the paper prototype worked as a complete device-free response?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Yes. All three testers completed it and marked an exact location.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: I agree with that observation. We also agree that two completed QR responses added later explanations.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: And one QR attempt stopped during a connection failure. Those are the shared facts.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: We still disagree about how strongly those facts support an optional digital stage.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Right. I’m open to another internal check, but I’m not agreeing to public adoption.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: For now, let’s test question clarity and completion with five independent staff members.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: The paper form would remain the complete default, and the QR questions would be clearly optional and unlinked.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: No names, contact details or candidate-material comments. We should also test the connection before anyone begins.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Good. That gives us a limited purpose, defined materials and a technical check.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I’ll summarize what we’ve decided. I own the two prototype drafts, due Tuesday at noon.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: I’ll review the privacy wording by three on Tuesday. That review depends on seeing the final questions.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I’ll run the five-person internal check on Thursday and record completion, time, location detail and any interruption.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: What result would make us revisit the optional stage?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: If the wording is understood, the connection is stable and at least four testers complete it, I’ll support discussing a later visitor trial.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That would still be a discussion, not automatic approval.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Understood. We seem to agree that the test can inform another decision, not make the public decision itself.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: We still disagree about whether QR is likely to be worth keeping, and the new evidence may narrow that gap.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The only open point is what happens after the internal report. We can revisit that when the report exists.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Then I’ll send one decision record today with the agreement, the disagreement, the owners and the review condition.
